title: Control Board Fault
fullDescription:
F0 on Kenmore ovens indicates a generic fault reported by the electronic oven control (EOC).

It may be a stuck key or a failed board.

Start by inspecting the touchpad before replacing electronics.

fixSteps.title: Inspect touchpad
fixSteps.instruction: Look for damage or sticky residue.

title: EEPROM Control Failure
shortDescription: Control board EEPROM or watchdog fault.
fullDescription:
F1 indicates the control board self-check has failed. The oven will shut down for safety.

Usually resolved by replacing the electronic oven control.

faq.a: Yes but oven cannot be used.

title: Oven Over Temperature
fullDescription:
F2 indicates the oven has exceeded a safe temperature. The control shuts off bake and broil elements.

Often caused by a stuck relay or faulty sensor.

fixSteps.title: Test RTD sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Should read ~1080 ohms at room temp.

whenToCallPro: Always if smoke or overheat persists.

faq.a: Yes, stop using the oven until repaired.

title: Open Temperature Sensor
fullDescription:
F3 means the oven temperature sensor circuit is open. The control cannot read temperature and disables heating.

Replace the RTD probe.

fixSteps.title: Access sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove sensor from rear wall of oven.

whenToCallPro: If wiring damage inside oven cavity.

faq.q: Is it safe to use stovetop?
faq.a: Yes, stovetop is separate from oven fault.

title: Shorted Sensor
fullDescription:
F4 indicates the oven sensor is shorted out. The board reads an impossibly high temperature.

Replace the RTD sensor.
whenToCallPro: If sensor new and fault persists.

title: Watchdog Circuit Fault
fullDescription: F5 signifies the watchdog circuit has tripped. This can be due to voltage issues or a failed EOC.
whenToCallPro: If board swap does not help.

title: Line Frequency Error
shortDescription: Incoming power frequency out of range.
fullDescription: F6 means the control cannot detect a stable 60Hz line frequency. Could be power quality or board fault.

fixSteps.title: Replace control
fixSteps.instruction: Install new EOC if wiring OK.

title: Stuck Key Error
shortDescription: A key on touchpad is stuck.
fullDescription: F7 indicates a stuck key on the touchpad. Residue, damage, or membrane failure can cause this.

title: Analog to Digital Fault
fullDescription: F8 indicates a failure in the control board analog-to-digital conversion. The board cannot translate sensor signals properly.

faq.a: Yes, if oven alone is affected.

title: Door Lock Error
fullDescription: F9 means the oven door latch motor or switches are not confirming lock status. This is important for self-clean cycles.

fixSteps.title: Access latch assembly
fixSteps.instruction: Remove top panel for door latch access.

faq.a: May need to wait for cool down or professional help.

title: Runaway Temperature
fullDescription: F10 indicates runaway temperature. The oven is heating without control input. This is a serious fault requiring immediate attention.
whenToCallPro: Highly recommended due to safety risk.

title: Shorted Keypad
fullDescription: F11 indicates a keypad short. The control can't operate normally because the ribbon signal is stuck low.

fixSteps.title: Disconnect keypad
fixSteps.instruction: If F11 clears, keypad is bad.
